analysis: Two things drove the mid-morning tape: a hot services-PMI read and the 10Y spiking to a 19-year high (5.06%, +9bp). The PMI numbers conflict across sources — IBD's '57 vs 53.9 Aug, est. 53.6' against the flash composite 53.6 reported this morning — so treat the exact figure as noise and the direction as signal: bonds read it hot, and rate-sensitive small caps led the drop (Russell -1%+). October-hike repricing is back in focus after yesterday's Nasdaq record. Memory names (SNDK, MU, DRAM ETF, SOXX) are digesting two strong days — healthy consolidation as long as SNDK holds its 1,827.99 early entry and MU's breakout holds; a failure there would turn profit-taking into distribution. Mag-7 divergence is the tape's other story: META (+1.5%) is bid into tonight's Connect keynote while GOOGL (-3%) drags MAGS, with no specific driver in sourced coverage. Oil above $100 keeps the energy-inflation headline risk alive ahead of today's EIA report. Thursday's Trump-Xi summit — with AI on the agenda and Musk attending the state dinner — is the next macro headline risk for NVDA/AAPL and China-exposed names. No HN/Reddit threads added signal beyond the headlines.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.why_it_matters: Event bid ahead of Connect — investors front-running expected camera-free Luna glasses and Muse AI announcements; reaction to tonight's reveals sets the tone.
